Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-30 09:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Evan Torres, Maya Li, Jordan Price, Sam Bennett (NovaCore)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, um, quick agenda \u0014 marketplace listing flow, the RA for private deployments, SSO/KMS and VPC connectivity, and next steps.
[00:12] Evan Torres: Yep sounds good, we mostly want to understand the ops burden and what NovaCore needs to provide for the listing, and also the joint solution bundle that shows up in the marketplace.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Great, I'll start on the tech side. So high level, Redwood supports three deployment modes for partners: hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC/on-prem). For a marketplace listing we typically show the reference architecture for both hosted integration and private deployment patterns.
[00:35] Jordan Price: Quick Q \u0014 do we need to containerize or provide terraform for the listing? Our internal marketplace expects a manifest and an image.
[00:44] Alex Kim: For NovaCore, the minimum is a manifest + listing assets (screenshots, pricing). We recommend providing a terraform module or helm chart for private deployments so customers can spin up the connector. But it's optional for hosted listings.
[00:57] Maya Li: When you say connector, do you mean the VPC peering connector and the SSO setup? How opinionated is Redwood there?
[01:06] Priya Shah: Right, that's the tricky bit. For private deployments we show an RA that includes a control plane (Redwood-managed or partner-managed) and a data path that stays in customer VPC. The network pieces: VPC peering / AWS PrivateLink or a transit gateway, plus a small bootstrap agent we recommend packaging. Sometimes the transcription will read private- uh, private plane \u0014 but yes the agent handles KV cache priming and auth handshake.
[01:28] Sam Bennett: Security \u0014 we need to know about KMS and HSM support. Our legal team is asking about where keys live, SOC 2, audit logs.
[01:36] Priya Shah: Redwood supports KMS integrations \u0014 AWS KMS and customer HSMs \u0014 and you can choose to bring-your-own-key. Audit logs are available via the Console; we also expose per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns. We'll share the security doc.
[01:47] Evan Torres: Are those logs stored in Redwood's control plane for hosted customers? Any residency concerns we should flag for the marketplace buyers?
[01:54] Alex Kim: For hosted, logs and metadata live in Redwood control plane in the region you pick; we have options for retention and for private deployments the logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM. We'll add a blurb in the RA about log forwarding and encryption at rest, um, so buyers know what to expect.
[02:10] Jordan Price: On billing & revenue share \u0014 marketplace requires us to specify billing cadence and possible revenue splits. Do you support metered billing via the marketplace?
[02:18] Alex Kim: Yes, Redwood's hosted API is usage-based and we can support metered consumption through the marketplace integration. For Dedicated and Private we usually do a contract-based pricing, and marketplace listings will call that out as enterprise-only with contact sales.
[02:30] [Speaker 3]: (mumbled) \u0014 I think we need a clear matrix in the listing: features, SLA, pricing bands.
[02:35] Priya Shah: Agreed. We'll create a short features matrix: hosted vs dedicated vs private, typical throughput (tokens/sec) and latency SLO, and recommended deployment pattern. We'll attach that to the listing assets.
[02:46] Maya Li: Technical deep dive \u0014 connectivity. For on-prem customers, do you support air-gapped installs? We have some banks asking for that.
[02:54] Priya Shah: Yes, we have an on-prem package; it's heavier because you need local model hosting and optional offline KMS/HSM. We'll include the RA for an air-gapped flow but note the support overhead.
[03:07] Evan Torres: Can Redwood provide a reference terraform module we can embed in our marketplace artifacts?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: We have partner terraform modules in our partner repo, yep. We'll share a sample module and a recommended manifest that NovaCore can use.
[03:20] Jordan Price: On the listing UI, we want an image and a short 'what you'll get' blurb plus a link to docs. What's the typical turnaround?
[03:28] Alex Kim: If you give us the assets we can draft the listing in 2-3 business days and iterate. The checklist I'm going to send includes required fields.
[03:35] [00:03:40] Sam Bennett: About SSO \u0014 we need SAML or OIDC, and we'd like SCIM for provisioning.
[03:42] Priya Shah: Redwood supports SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. For marketplace buyer flows we usually recommend SAML for enterprise customers. We'll attach sample metadata and an example IdP config.
[03:51] Evan Torres: Can you confirm whether KV cache and batching are preserved in private deployments? One of our customers is latency sensitive and they worry about token costs.
[03:59] Priya Shah: Yes, the runtime's KV cache and batching are available in Dedicated and Private. For quantized models we recommend the 4-bit quant profile for cost reduction; the RA will show tradeoffs. Expect slightly different throughput numbers on CPU vs GPU.
[04:17] Jordan Price: Any worries about model licensing for marketplace? We want to surface which models are available in hosted vs on-prem.
[04:24] Alex Kim: We'll include a model catalog callout in the listing. For hosted we can expose curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For private/on-prem, customers need to provide or license models, or use our recommended images where licensing allows.
[04:39] [00:04:40] Maya Li: Okay on integration steps \u0014 what do you need from NovaCore for the prototype?
[04:45] Alex Kim: Sandbox creds for your marketplace, a sample manifest, and a contact for billing. Priya will need a test IdP for SSO and optionally KMS test creds for a spike.
[04:54] Priya Shah: I'll also run a short spike to validate the VPC connector and the SSO handshake, record steps and send screenshots. Likely a half day to spin up and test. If we hit networking oddities it can take longer.
[05:06] Evan Torres: Great. On the joint solution \u0014 can we include a reference architecture doc and a short 'getting started' playbook for customers who buy via the marketplace?
[05:14] Alex Kim: Absolutely. We'll draft a 2-page RA and a 1-page quickstart. We'll also include the rollout plan: canary deploys, A/B test notes, and fallback options if the partner's capacity is constrained.
[05:25] Sam Bennett: Security quick note \u0014 ensure the RA mentions SOC 2 and audit logs, and show where audit trails live. We'll need that for our compliance review.
[05:33] Alex Kim: Noted. We'll add a compliance appendix.
[05:36] [00:05:37] Jordan Price: Are there any blockers or major dev work on Redwood's side to get the listing live?
[05:42] Priya Shah: Mostly doc and sample artifacts. If NovaCore needs deep integration like on-prem image signing or custom HSM flows, that could be a bit more work. But for the standard listing \u0014 manifest + terraform + SSO sample \u0014 that's straightforward.
[05:56] Evan Torres: Timeline \u0014 we'd like to get a basic listing in the marketplace in April. Hoping for a 2-3 week turnaround. Is that feasible?
[06:03] Alex Kim: Yes, if we get the sandbox creds and assets early April we can aim for a mid-April listing. We'll write that in the next steps.
[06:10] Priya Shah: I'll put together the prototype steps and ETA in the doc I send.
[06:14] [00:06:15] Alex Kim: Alright let's recap quick: Alex to share checklist and sample RA by 4/2; Priya to do SSO/KMS/VPC spike and share findings by 4/9; NovaCore to provide sandbox creds + manifest by 4/5; Jordan to confirm revenue share by 4/6. We'll schedule a follow-up demo once checklist updates are in.
[06:33] Maya Li: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:36] Evan Torres: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:38] Alex Kim: Thanks all \u0014 ending now.
